title: Specialiseret butiksmedarbejder/knivspecialist. Specialist retail assistent - Japanese as working language
description:
Arbejdssted: København Location: Copenhagen

Arbejdstid: Fuldtid 37 timer om ugen. Working hours. Full-time, 37 hours per week.

Ansættelsesform: Fastansættelse Employment: Permanent position.

Om stillingen:

Vi søger en engageret medarbejder til vores specialiserede butik med fokus på japanske kvalitetsknive og japansk knivhåndværk.

Stillingen er en kombination af salg og kundeservice, arbejde med slibning af knive samt løbende kontakt med vores japanske leverandører og samarbejdspartnere.

Stillingen kombinerer salg og kundeservice med praktisk arbejde, slibning og vedligeholdelse af knive samt løbende kontakt med vores japanske leverandører og samarbejdspartnere.

En væsentlig del af stillingen indebærer direkte kommunikation med japanske producenter og leverandører. Derfor er gode japanske sprogkundskaber en nødvendighed kompetence i stillingen.

Dine arbejdsopgaver:

Salg og rådgivning af kunder om japanske kvalitetsknive og tilbehør.

Kundeservice og vejledning om valg, brug og vedligeholdelse af knive.

Slibning og vedligeholdelse af knive, samt indgravering i hånden.

Modtagelse, kontrol og håndtering af varer.

Vare- og lagerstyring.

Kommunikation med japanske leverandører og producenter,

Håndtering af profuktinformation, ordrer, specifikationer og leverancer.

Oversættelse og videreformidling af information mellem virksomheden og japanske leverandører.

Bidrage til den daglige drift og præsentation af butikken.

Vi forventer, at du:

Taler og skriver japansk på højt niveau.

Kan kommunikere proffesionelt med vores japanske leverandører både mundtligt og skriftligt.

Har interesse for japanske knive, håndværk og kvalitet.

Har gode kundeservice- og salgsevner.

Er omhyggelig og kvalitetsbevidst.

Kan arbejde selvstændigt og tage ansvar.

Har interesse for eller erfaring med knivslibning.

Behersker engelsk, så du kan kommunikere med kolleger og kunder.

Erfaring med knivslibning, salg eller arbejde med japanske knive er en fordel. Erfaring med håndgravering er ligeledes en fordel. Oplæring i virksomhedens produkter og arbejdsmetoder vil blive givet efter behov.

Japansk er et nødvendigt arbejdssprog, da medarbejderne vil have løbende kontakt med japanske producenter og leverandører, vedrørende blandt andet produktinformation, bestillinger, specifikationer og leverancer.

Vi tilbyder:

Fast ansættelse på 37 timer om ugen.

En alsidig stilling i en specialiseret butik.

Arbejde med japanske kvalitetsprodukter og knivhåndværk.

Direkte kontakt med japanske producenter og leverandører.

Oplæring i produkter, knivtyper og slibeteknikker.

Et arbejdsmiljø med fokus på kvalitet, faglighed og god kundeservice.

Løn: Efter aftale.

Ansøgning:

Send CV og ansøgning til tess@foodgear.dk.

Fortæl gerne om din baggrund og erfaring med japansk håndværk, samt dine sprogkundskaber.

Regarding the position:

We are looking for an enthusiastic and service-minded employee to join our specialized shop, focusing on high quality Japanese knives and Japanese knife craftmanship.

The position combines sales and customer service with practical work, involving knife sharpening and maintenance, as well as ongoing communication with our Japanese suppliers and business partners.

A significant part of the postion involves direct communication with Japanese manufacturers and suppliers. Therefore, a high level of Japanese language proficiency is an essential requirement for the position.

Your responsibilities:

Selling and advising customers on Japanese high quality knives and accessories.

Providing customer service andguidance on the selection, use and maintenance of knives.

Knife sharpening, maintenance and hand engraving.

Receiving, checking and handling goods.

Stock and inventory management.

Communication with Japanese suppliers and manufacturers.

Handling product information, orders, specifications and deliveries.

Translating and communicating information between the company and Japanese business partners.

Contributing to the day-to-day operation and presentation of the shop.

We expect you to:

Speak and write Japanese at a high level.

Be able to communicate professionally with Japanese suppliers, both verbally and in writing.

Have an interest in Japanese knives, craftmanship and quality.

Have good customer service and sales skills.

Be detail oriented and quality conscious.

Be able to work independently and take responsibility.

Have an interest in or experience with knife sharpening.

Have a good command of English for communication with colleagues and customers.

Experience in sales, knife sharpening or working with Japaneseknives is an advantage. Experience with hand engraving of knives is also an advantage. Training in the companys products and working methods will be provided as required.

Japanese is an essential working language, as the employee will have regular contact with Japanese manufacturers and suppliers regarding product information, orders, specifikations, deliveries and other matters related to our Japanese products.

We offer:

A permanent full-time position of 37 hours per week.

A varied position in a specialised retail shop.

The opportunity to work with high-quality Japanese products and traditional knife craftmanship.

Direct contact with Japanese manufacturers and suppliers.

Training in products, knife types and sharpening techniques.

A working environment focused on quality, expertise and excellent customer service.

Salary: Salary and employment terms according to qualifications and experience.

How to apply: Please send an email with your CV and application to tess@foodgear.dk

Please include information about your experience with Japanese products, knives, sales, customer service as well as your Japanese and English skills.

title: PhD Stipend in Digital Twin Modelling and Multi-Timescale Optimization of Electrolysis Systems
description:
Help to build the digital backbone of tomorrow's Power-to-X plants. This 3-year PhD position offers a unique opportunity to build a research career at the intersection of digital twins, multi-timescale optimization, and integrated Power-to-X systems. You will drive the development of system-level digital-twin and optimization methodologies, integrating electrolyzer models with renewable generation, power conversion, energy and hydrogen storage, downstream processes, and energy demand, to enable more efficient, flexible, and economically viable Power-to-X operation. This position is expected to start from 1st of November 2026 or as soon as possible hereafter.

About the project
The position is affiliated with the Pioneer Center for Accelerating P2X Materials Discovery (CAPeX) and the section for Applied Power Electronic Systems. You will join an interdisciplinary team working across electrolysers, Power-to-X systems, power electronics, control, digital twins, and energy-system optimization, in close collaboration with the Technical University of Denmark (DTU), University of Toronto, Stanford University, and Utrecht University, and research visits to partner facilities may form part of the position.

Your work tasks
You will develop and validate digital-twin and optimization methods for electrolysis systems, working both independently and collaboratively with the group and with academic and industrial partners. In particular, you will:

  • Develop and validate physics-based, data-driven, or hybrid digital twins of Electrolysis systems, capturing their electrochemical, thermal, flow, and system-level behaviour for system monitoring, state estimation, and performance prediction.
  • Build computationally efficient models suitable for monitoring, performance prediction, optimization, and control, and evaluate their accuracy, robustness, computational efficiency, and practical applicability. They could also be implemented in real-time systems.
  • Investigate interactions across operational timescales (Multi-timescale optimization) — from short-term power, thermal, and flow management to longer-term production scheduling and energy-system operation — connecting fast system dynamics with slower operational decisions.
  • Develop optimization strategies to improve Electrolyzer performance, efficiency, flexibility, and economic operation under variable electricity supply and renewable-energy integration.
  • Collaborate with academic and industrial partners and disseminate results through scientific publications, conferences, and project activities.

The position may also include a limited amount of teaching and supervision of bachelor's and master's students in areas related to your expertise.

Your competencies 
We expect you to have:

  • A relevant master's degree in energy engineering, electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, chemical engineering, control engineering, or a related discipline.
  • A strong foundation in at least one of: electrochemical or energy-system modelling, dynamic modelling and control, mathematical optimization, or data-driven modelling.
  • Experience with numerical modelling, simulation, optimization, control, or engineering-data analysis.
  • Good programming skills in Python, MATLAB/Simulink, or a comparable scientific computing environment.
  • A fundamental understanding of energy-conversion systems, thermodynamics, electrical engineering, heat and mass transfer, electrochemistry, or control engineering.
  • The ability to conduct independent, systematic, and scientifically rigorous research while working effectively in a multidisciplinary team.
  • Good written and spoken English.

Experience with some of the areas of electrolyzer technologies, digital twins, model order reduction, system identification, power electronics, model predictive control, multi-objective optimization, machine learning, renewable-energy integration, experimental testing, or hardware-in-the-loop implementation would be an advantage. You are not expected to have expertise in all of these areas.

Qualification requirements
PhD stipends are allocated to individuals who hold a Master's degree. PhD stipends are normally for a period of 3 years. It is a prerequisite for allocation of the stipend that the candidate will be enrolled as a PhD student at the Doctoral School of Engineering and Science in accordance with the regulations of Ministerial Order No. 1124 of September 19, 2025 on the PhD Programme at the Universities and Certain Higher Artistic Educational Institutions. According to the Ministerial Order, the progress of the PhD student shall be assessed at regular points in time. As part of the PhD study, you are among other things required to complete PhD courses corresponding to 30 ECTS, gain experience with teaching or other forms of knowledge dissemination and complete an external research stay outside of Aalborg University, preferably 3-6 months at a foreign research institution.

Who we are
The PhD Student will be positioned to the section for “Applied Power Electronic Systems” at Department of Energy in Aalborg University (AAU Energy). AAU Energy is an international research department at Aalborg University dedicated to developing clean and sustainable energy systems across electrical, thermal, and mechatronic energy technologies. We offer an interdisciplinary research environment, advanced laboratory facilities, and extensive collaboration with industry and academic partners. The department has campuses in Aalborg and Esbjerg; this position is based in Aalborg.

We offer access to advanced laboratory and workshop facilities and an environment where you can develop your academic profile through research, teaching and collaboration with both Danish and international external partners. As a workplace we value a collegial and inclusive culture with room for professional discussion, initiative and mutual support in everyday work.

New colleagues, whether they come from elsewhere in Denmark or from abroad, can draw on the university’s support services related to relocation, housing and practical matters. Aalborg University offers general onboarding support to all new employees, as well as dedicated support for international staff through its International Staff Unit (ISU). You can read more about relocation support and services here: https://www.en.hr.aau.dk/relocation-support

Aalborg University also offers Danish language courses to support international employees in settling into both the workplace and Danish society. International employees typically can attend Danish language courses during their first years in Denmark (depending on individual eligibility and national schemes).

You can read more about AAU Energy at www.energy.aau.dk.

How to apply
Your application must include the following:

  • Application, stating reasons for applying and qualifications in relation to the position
  • Curriculum Vitae (CV)
  • Diplomas (bachelor's and master's degree diploma, including grades) 
  • A project description (3–5 pages) outlining your initial thoughts and ideas on the project applied for, including a brief state-of-the-art with a short list of references, a time schedule, and how you intend to address the project objectives.
  • Publications, if applicable.
  • Other relevant documents

The application must be submitted via Aalborg University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aalborg University's website. 

Aalborg University wants to reflect the surrounding society and has diversity as a core value. Therefore, everyone, regardless of personal background and orientation, is encouraged to apply for the position.

Do you have any questions?     
If you have any questions about the position, you are more than welcome to contact us. You will find contact persons at the bottom of the jobpost.

Further information  
Read more about our recruitment process here.

The assessment of candidates for the position will be carried out by qualified experts.
Shortlisting will be applied. This means that after the application deadline, the head of the department, with the assistance of the hiring committee, will select the applicants to be assessed. All applicants will be informed whether they have been shortlisted for assessment or not.

The hiring process at Aalborg University may include a risk assessment as a tool to identify potential risks associated with new hires, ensuring the safety, compliance, and integrity of the workplace.

Read more about The Doctoral School of Engineering and Science

Salary and terms of employment
The employment is in accordance with the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities and the Ministerial Order on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities. Furthermore, your terms of employment and salary are in accordance with the collective agreement between the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations and the state (AC collective agreement). 

You can find information about the salary and salary structure for the position in the Salary Overview for Recruitment - Scientific positions (VIP). Please refer to the introductory section of the page and the section entitled “PhD Fellow”.

title: Postdoc Position in System Optimization Using Digital Twin for Power-to-X processes
description:
Take the next step in your research career at the intersection of digital twins, multi-timescale system optimization, and integrated Power-to-X systems with special focus on the electrical engineering parts. This position offers a unique opportunity to drive the development of system-level digital-twin and optimization methodologies—integrating electrolyzer models with renewable generation, power electronic conversion, energy and hydrogen storage, downstream processes, and energy demand—to enable more efficient, flexible, and economically viable Power-to-X operation. This position is expected to start from 1st of November 2026 or as soon as possible hereafter.

About the project
The position is affiliated with the Pioneer Center for Accelerating P2X Materials Discovery (CAPeX) and the section for Applied Power Electronic Systems. You will join an interdisciplinary team working across electrolyzers, Power-to-X systems, power electronics, control, digital twins, and energy-system optimization, in close collaboration with the Technical University of Denmark (DTU), University of Toronto, Stanford University, and Utrecht University — research visits to partner facilities may form part of the position.

Your work tasks
This two-year postdoctoral project focuses on the system-level integration and optimization of electrolyzer digital twins within CAPeX — considering how component-level electrolyzer models and digital twins can be incorporated into broader Power-to-X systems involving renewable generation, power conversion, power system integration, energy and hydrogen storage, downstream processes, and energy demand. In particular, you will:

  • Develop an integrated, system-level digital-twin framework connecting electrolyzer models with relevant Power-to-X components and energy-systema.
  • Develop system-level optimization and energy-management methods for coordinating electrolyzers with renewable generation, power conversion, storage, downstream processes, and hydrogen demand.
  • Apply and evaluate these methods under technical constraints and varying renewable generation, electricity prices, and hydrogen demand, considering system efficiency, flexibility, production, and operating costs.
  • Validate and benchmark the developed framework using project data, high-fidelity simulations including hardware in the loop, and relevant industrial case studies, assessing its robustness and computational performance.
  • Collaborate with researchers and industrial partners, contribute to the coordination and supervision of related research activities, and disseminate results through scientific publications, conferences, and project deliverables.

The position may also include a limited amount of teaching and supervision of bachelor's and master's students in areas related to your expertise.

Your competencies
We expect you to have:

  • A PhD in electrical engineering, energy engineering, mechanical engineering, control engineering, operations research, applied mathematics, or a closely related field.
  • Documented experience in energy-system modelling, mathematical optimization, control, digital twins, or related areas.
  • Strong programming and numerical modelling skills using Python, MATLAB/Simulink, Julia, hardware in the loop implementation or comparable tools.
  • Experience with one or more relevant methods, such as multi-objective optimization, model predictive control, mixed-integer optimization, stochastic optimization, energy management, or production scheduling.
  • Good knowledge of integrated energy systems; experience with electrolyzers, hydrogen technologies, renewable-energy integration, storage, or Power-to-X systems would be an advantage.
  • A strong scientific publication record appropriate to your career stage.
  • The ability to conduct independent research, collaborate across disciplines, and communicate effectively with academic and industrial partners.
  • Excellent written and spoken English.

You are not expected to be a specialist in every electrolyzer technology or optimization method. Strong system-level modelling and optimization competence, together with the ability to work across component and system boundaries, is particularly important.

Who we are
The position will be based in the section for “Applied Power Electronic Systems” at Department of Energy in Aalborg University (AAU Energy). AAU Energy is an international research department at Aalborg University dedicated to developing clean and sustainable energy systems across electrical, thermal, and mechatronic energy technologies. We offer an interdisciplinary research environment, advanced laboratory facilities, and extensive collaboration with industry and academic partners. The department has campuses in Aalborg and Esbjerg; this position is based in Aalborg. Read more at www.energy.aau.dk.

Qualification requirements
Appointment as postdoc requires academic qualifications at PhD level.

How to apply  
Your application must include the following:

title: Kontorleder søges
description:
OFFICE MANAGER WANTED FOR OUR OFFICE IN ØSTERBRO

Are you service-minded, organised, and the kind of person who keeps the office running smoothly – even when things get busy?

We are looking for a dedicated Office Manager for a permanent position at our office in Østerbro, Copenhagen.

As our Office Manager, you will be a central part of our day-to-day operations and play an important role in ensuring that the office runs professionally and efficiently.

We operate a staffing agency where the pace can be fast. Phones are ringing, candidates are coming and going, and there are always people, appointments, and tasks that need to be coordinated.

That is why we are looking for someone who thrives on responsibility, enjoys working with people, and appreciates a varied working day.

YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES

You will be responsible for the day-to-day running of the office. Your responsibilities will include:

title: Postdoctoral Position in Animal Welfare Risks of Feeding Red Seaweed to Dairy Cows
description:
The Department of Animal and Veterinary Sciences, Aarhus University, calls for applications for a full-time postdoctoral position. The two-year position is available from 1 February 2027, or soon thereafter. The position will be in the research unit Behaviour, stress and welfare (BSW).

Dairy cattle contribute substantially to agricultural greenhouse gas emissions, primarily through enteric methane production, making the identification of effective nutritional mitigation strategies an important area of research. While the feed additive Bovaer has received considerable attention for its methane-reducing effects, concerns regarding animal health and welfare have led to increasing interest in alternative solutions, including seaweed-based feed additives. The seaweed Asparagopsis spp. has shown significant methane-mitigating potential; however, its use has also raised animal welfare concerns. Consequently, there is a need to evaluate the animal welfare effects of seaweed-based feed additives.

Research tasks
  • Evaluating the effects of seaweed-based feed additives on the behaviour and welfare of dairy cattle.
  • Investigating behavioural indicators of discomfort and pain associated with feed management.
  • Validating welfare assessment measures through experimental approaches, including pharmacological interventions.
  • Contributing to scientific publications and dissemination of research results.
  • Participating in knowledge exchange activities with public authorities and industry stakeholders.
  • Contributing to teaching and supervision of students at the bachelor's, master's, and PhD levels.


Qualifications
We are seeking a candidate who has:
  • A PhD degree or equivalent in biology, animal science, veterinary science, or a related field, and research experience in animal behaviour and welfare.
  • A strong interest in strategies aimed at reducing the climate impact of dairy production through feeding management.
  • At least a basic understanding of feeding management.
  • Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to communicate scientific research results effectively.
  • The ability to work independently as well as collaboratively in a research environment.
  • For non-Scandinavian candidates, a commitment to learning Danish, including reading, writing, and speaking, is expected during the employment period.


Contact
Further information on the position may be obtained from Professor Margit Bak Jensen, phone: +4522365482, email: margitbak.jensen@anivet.au.dk

What we offer
  • A well-developed research infrastructure, laboratories and access to shared equipment and animal experimental facilities
  • An informal and multicultural research environment with high professionalism and close collaboration and networking activities
  • A workplace characterized by equality and a good work-life balance, and an open discussion across different fields of research.


The candidate will have the opportunity to be trained and gain experience in:
  • Teaching and supervision of students at the BSc and MSc level through active involvement in teaching in animal science and in the veterinary science programme.
  • Research-based consultancy to authorities, where it is relevant.


Who we are
Department of Animal and Veterinary Sciences is well-known for its skilled and very innovative interdisciplinary research environments with high international impact. We perform world-class research, which contributes with solutions to solve essential societal challenges within the green transition: food production and veterinary medicine – nationally and globally.

The department generates novel research at the highest international level within sustainable food production, environment, climate, health and welfare for animals and humans. The activities form the basis for the research-based public sector consultancy and degree programs covering bachelor’s, master’s and PhD degree programs within animal science and veterinary medicine. We offer a lively, engaged and innovative learning and study environment, which is closely integrated in the research environment.

Our department has unique and advanced animal experimental research facilities and technologies, situated in close connection to the research environment, and a comprehensive national and international research network and good industrial and professional collaboration.

Please refer to Department of Animal and Veterinary Sciences (au.dk) for further information about the department: https://anivet.au.dk/en

Place of work and area of employment
The place of work is the Department of Animal and Veterinary Sciences, AU Viborg,
Blichers Allé 20, DK-8830 Tjele, and the area of employment is Aarhus University (AU) with related departments.

Living in Denmark
Please visit the international staff website: https://internationalstaff.au.dk/prearrival/ for information about arriving to and living in Denmark for both the applicants and their potential families.



Application procedure
Shortlisting is used. This means that after the deadline for applications – and with the assistance from the assessment committee chairman, and the appointment committee if necessary, – the head of department selects the candidates to be evaluated. All applicants will be notified whether or not their applications have been sent to an expert assessment committee for evaluation. The selected applicants will be informed about the composition of the committee, and each applicant is given the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that concerns him/her self.



Formalities and salary range
Technical Sciences refers to the Ministerial Order on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Danish Universities under the Danish Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation.

The application must be in English and include a curriculum vitae, degree certificate, a complete list of publications, a statement of future research plans and information about research activities, teaching portfolio and verified information on previous teaching experience (if any). Guidelines for applicants can be found here.

Appointment shall be in accordance with the collective labour agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Further information on qualification requirements and job content may be found in the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff at Danish Universities.

Salary and terms as agreed between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions at basic salary steps 4-8.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

Research activities will be evaluated in relation to actual research time. Thus, we encourage applicants to specify periods of leave without research activities, in order to be able to subtract these periods from the span of the scientific career during the evaluation of scientific productivity.

Aarhus University offers a broad variety of services for international researchers and accompanying families, including relocation service and career counselling to expat partners. Read more here. Please find more information about entering and working in Denmark here.

Aarhus University also offers a Junior Researcher Development Programme targeted at career development for postdocs at AU. You can read more about it here.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

title: Junior Software Developer
description:
Want to work with sustainability and software? Looking to be part of an innovative, fast-growing Danish greentech company with global reach? Then Explicit might be the place for you.

We are looking for a software developer to join us to develop and maintain our digital platforms as we scale.

We do drone-based emissions monitoring across oil & gas, maritime, waste management, and other industries. By helping operators safely identify methane leaks and quantify emissions, we're proud to be supporting industry efforts to improve environmental performance while enhancing operational efficiency and asset integrity. We measure greenhouse gas emissions data from various sources and combining them with atmospheric data. Based on scientific methods we then quantify emissions and visualize the data to provide emissions intelligence to operations enabling actions on emissions.

We have a strong focus on R&D, and we are exploring new cutting-edge technologies and ideas to innovate what we can do within emissions monitoring.

The job

You will be part of a small, talented tech developer team, responsible for designing, building and maintaining our digital platforms, which are the core of the products we deliver to customers.

As a Software Developer your responsibilities will include:

  • Co-development of our main applications Microsoft Azure, Blazor Server Application (C#)

  • Co-development of our calculation engine, Microsoft Azure Function (Python)

  • Develop new, more appealing user experiences aimed at different user groups to view products and services.

  • Maintain databases, application services and reporting landscape specific to the European maritime emission monitoring set-up.

  • Improve analysis tools and the user experience for the customers, the drone pilot and the internal project manager in collaboration with the project manager running the campaigns.

About you

We are looking for a candidate who meets the following criteria:

  • A bachelor's degree or master’s degree in engineering, data science, software design, computer engineering, mathematics, physics or similar

  • Experience with code development in C# and Python and preferable Rust

  • Experience with database design (SQL)

  • Familiar with software development processes in Azure DevOps

  • Experience with development of user interfaces and UX design is an advantage, but not a requirement

  • Fluent in English. Danish is an advantage, but not a requirement

  • Genuine interest in technology and IT infrastructure

  • Structured and focused on delivering quality work and being a good team player.

 

What we offer

  • A permanent, full-time position in a fast-growing greentech company with real-world impact on cutting industrial emissions

  • Competitive benefits including paid pension, health insurance, parental leave and 6 weeks' holiday allowance

  • Software ownership early on, with senior developers to learn from

  • A flat hierarchy where ideas are heard, initiative is encouraged, and responsibility comes early

  • A supportive team that values collaboration, trust and learning

  • Job location is just north of Copenhagen in Virum, Denmark.

Application and information

We encourage you to apply as soon as possible, as we will be evaluating applications on an ongoing basis. Application deadline is 18 October 2026. Expected start date is 1 November 2026.

Please send your application, including your motivation and what a competence you bring, together with your CV to jobs@explicit.dk. Write “Software developer” in the subject field.

If you have any questions about the job, you are welcome to contact Rasmus Ebdrup, Chief Digital Officer at reb@explicit.dk

___________________________________________________________________________________

About Explicit

Explicit ApS is a pioneering Danish green tech company specialising in drone-based emissions monitoring across the energy, maritime, waste management, and other industries. We deliver reliable, transparent and actionable emissions data to some of the largest energy companies all over the world using our patented drone-based methodology.

We are headquartered in Virum, Denmark, with offices in Norway, Germany and Australia. Our international team of around 30 colleagues brings together engineering, data and environmental expertise, united by a shared mission to make a difference in emissions monitoring. Read more about what we do at explicit.dk

title: Pædagogisk assistent til vuggestue
description:
Børnehytten søger en dedikeret pædagogisk assistent til vores vuggestue.

Hvem er vi: 

Vi er en privat integreret daginstitution beliggende i hjertet af Kettinge. Vi er normeret til 12 vuggestuebørn og 29 børnehavebørn. Vi har tæt samarbejde med forældrebestyrelse og det lokale forenings- og forretningsliv.

Huset rummer nærhed, omsorg og sammenhold for børnene såvel som for kollegaerne. Vi har fokus på trivsel og tryghed og vægter derfor bl.a. forældrekontakten højt. Vi er gode til at arbejde sammen og spille hinanden gode i hverdagen. Grundet husets størrelse er der en naturlig god relation til børnene på tværs af stuerne og vi kan hurtigt træde til på alle stuer, hvis behovet opstår. 

Børnehytten støder op til en tidligere grusgrav, der nu fungerer som rekreativt område med bålhytte, naturlegeplads, kunstige søer med fisk og mange andre muligheder for udfoldelser med børnene. Derudover har vi vores egen legeplads der er opdelt i vuggestue og børnehave, hvor vi prioriterer at børnene kommer ud hver dag. Det er derfor vigtigt, at du nyder at være en del af udelivet uanset vind og vejr, da vores børn også elsker at hoppe i vandpytter, kigge på biller og finde regnorme.

I vuggestuen er værdien af tid central for vores pædagogiske arbejde. Tid til nærvær, tid til fordybelse og tid til at skabe små betydningsfulde øjeblikke der danner fundamentet for børnenes læring, udvikling, trivsel og dannelse. Vi har fokus på at skabe udviklende læringsmiljøer, hvor alle børn – uanset behov og forudsætning -har mulighed for at deltage i meningsfulde fællesskaber.

Vi forventer af dig:

Du er uddannet pædagogisk assistent og gerne med erfaring fra dagtilbudsområdet. Du er empatisk, omsorgsfuld og vægter arbejdet med relationer højt. Du er nysgerrig og legende i din tilgang til børnene og vægter tid, tillid og tryghed højt hos både store og små.

Du skal have en naturlig interesse og nysgerrighed på sproglig udvikling og brugen af det i hverdagen.

Du kan i samarbejde med dine kollegaer på stuen, planlægge aktiviteter og evaluere disse med udgangspunkt i den nye styrkede pædagogiske læreplan.

Du kan samarbejde med din kollegaer, om at vurdere børnenes trivsel og udvikling og ved behov iværksætte konkrete tiltag. Du skal kunne se det enkelte barn og bidrage til at udarbejde handleplaner, indstillinger, koordinere tværfagligt samarbejde med mere.

 

Om stillingen:

Vi tilbyder en ansættelse hurtigst mulig eller fra 1/11-26 i en 32 timers stilling efter gld. overenskomst.

Ansøgningsfrist: 23/9-26 Samtaler forventes afholdt i uge 40.

Send din ansøgning og CV til leder@boernehytten.dk

 

Kontakt gerne leder: Tinni eller souschef Stine - 53841514 - Man-Fredag kl. 9-15, for mere information.

title: Postdoc Position (2 years) in Manufacturing Technology & Industrial Management
description:
The Department of Technology and Innovation (ITI) at University of Southern Denmark (SDU), section of Engineering Operations Management, invites applications for a 2-year position as Postdoc in Manufacturing Technology & Industrial Management.  The position is open from December 1, 2026, and the job location is Odense, Denmark.

 

Job description  

Successful candidates will drive internationally competitive research, collaborate in and across disciplines, work closely with industry and attract competitive external research and innovation funding in collaboration with senior researchers. The candidates will play a key role in providing outstanding education, supervise students, and develop junior research staff. 

 

We offer 

We offer a vigorous international research environment with a balance of male and female researchers, excellent facilities, including the new Robotics and Additive Manufacturing Laboratories at University of Southern Denmark, a long-term strategic initiative created to support research, teaching, and industrial collaboration and experimentation. SDU expects to increase its’ collaboration with industrial companies and associations in the coming years. 

This position will imply collaboration with industrial partners in the Renewable Energy Sector. Examples can be vendors of wind turbines, electrification solutions, electrolyzers, biogas equipment, carbon capture, utilization and storage technologies etc. It can also be major owners / operators of renewable energy plants, as offshore wind turbine park operators, green hydrogen / methanol / ammonia plants etc.

Research will be done to support DK and EU in realizing ambitions for production of green energy at off-take prices competitive with energy from fossil fuels via scaling and industrialization, whether the energy is in the form of green electricity or green fuels for industry and transport. There will be specific emphasis on research into the interplay between business strategy, product design, manufacturing systems design, manufacturing technology choices and scenarios or plans for industrial scaling. In addition to that, the position offers the opportunity to shape our educational and research and innovation programs by contributing to teaching and supervision in areas of Manufacturing technologies of the future and Industrial Management to benefit from new developments in research fields, approaches and content.   

 

We expect 

Candidates must have a relevant PhD.

Commensurate with the seniority of the position applied for, the candidates must ideally have: 

  • An excellent standing in research and innovation

  • Documented experience and good track record with education and supervision on undergraduate or graduate level

  • Extensive experience with industrial collaboration: can be from working in partnerships with or within companies, but also industrial and NGO organizations 

  • Industry outreach and work experience will be assessed positively 

  • Research & innovation project management experience will be assessed positively 

  • International work experience, organizational drive and a team-oriented mindset

  • Good written and oral communication skills

  • Fluent in English, both spoken and written                   

Candidates must have experience and competence in several, but not all, of the following fields: 

  • Business, Manufacturing and Operations Strategy

  • Product / Service design for Manufacturing, Logistics and Sustainability

  • Systems Design and Engineering

  • Materials Science, Industrial processes & Future Manufacturing Technologies

  • Design, Operations & Maintenance of Manufacturing Systems

  • Lean Manufacturing / Logistics and Industry 4.0 / 5.0 

  • Discrete Event Simulation Methods, Agent Based Simulation & Technologies

  • Machine Learning, AI, LLMs & Data Science for Manufacturing and Supply Chain Operations

  • Cost-Benefit and Return of Investment Analysis

  • Life Cycle Analysis Methods 

  • Modelling and Simulation methods

  • Case study, Design Science, Action Research Methods

  • Project Management, Agile Methods, Scrum Methods

  • EU strategies and plan for decarbonization of industry and society 

  • UN Sustainability Goals and Dimensions,

Working experience from industry, also within the renewable energy sector, will be seen as positive add-on but is not a requirement to apply for the position. 

 

Contact information
Further information about the position may be obtained from Head of Section, Niels Gorm Maly Rytter, phone: +45 29103729 or email: ngry@iti.sdu.dk 

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

 

Application

Applicants are advised to read the SDU information on how to apply.

Assessment of the candidates is based on the application material, and the application must include: 

  • Curriculum Vitae including information on previous employment, list of programming skills mastered by the applicant, and teaching and supervision experience.

  • Letter of motivation, including details on qualifications within the subject area (max. one page).

  • Master’s and PhD degree certificates or equivalent (original and an official English translation).  

  • Complete list of publications.

  • Publications most relevant to the position on which the applicant wishes to rely on.

  • Summary and documentation of experience in teaching. 

  • A research statement may be included.

  • At least one letter of recommendation from supervisors or previous employers. Should your referees wish to send their letters directly to us, please have them use e-mail: tek-hr@tek.sdu.dk mentioning your name and the title of the position in the subject line. Please note that these also need to reach us before deadline.

  • A statement/documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

 

The application deadline is October 15, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an expert or assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU.  Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. Read about the Assessment and selection process.  

 

Employment terms

Appointment as a postdoc is temporary for an initial 2-year period, and the preferred start date is from December 1, 2026. Extension may be possible depending on available funding.

Employment as a postdoc requires academic qualifications at PhD level at the time of employment. Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for postdoc as described therein. 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

-

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

Further information for international applicants about entering and working in Denmark. You may also visit WorkinDenmark for additional information.

title: PhD Position(s) in Computational Design and Robotic Fabrication for Timber Upcycling
description:
SDU CREATE invites highly motivated candidates who wish to contribute to a more sustainable built environment to apply for a PhD position in Computational Design and Robotic Fabrication for Timber Upcycling. The position(s) are expected to begin in January 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The application deadline is 15 October 2026 at 23:59 CEST.

 

Scope of the work

The PhD position(s) is linked to the Villum CEBE programme, Civil Engineering and the Green Transition in the Built Environment, funded by the Villum Foundation. Within Research Field 2, Design for Regeneration, Circularity and Longevity, the overall ambition is to extend the life cycle of reclaimed timber and retain its stored carbon for longer by transforming discarded wood into durable, materially efficient architectural components.

The research will investigate how heterogeneous pieces of waste timber can be reconstituted into engineered components with differentiated geometries and material properties. Computational design will connect architectural form, structural performance and available material stock, exploring how the arrangement, orientation and combination of reclaimed wood can generate new possibilities for building elements. The project will identify and develop suitable bonding techniques, integrate robotic fabrication with material characterisation, and demonstrate the resulting architectural systems at full scale.

We seek candidates with primary expertise in one of two complementary research profiles:

  • Computational Design and Robotic Fabrication: focusing on architectural design workflows, material allocation, robotic tooling, and the development of lamination, shaping and fabrication procedures for reclaimed timber.

  • AI-driven Computational Engineering: focusing on machine learning for material characterisation and property prediction, finite element modelling, structural optimisation, and experimental testing of timber, bonded interfaces and laminated components.

The successful candidate(s) will work within a team to develop and validate stock-informed design methods through computational investigation, hands-on fabrication experiments and full-scale architectural demonstrators. The candidate(s) will also contribute to the Centre’s activities, including teaching in the MSc CREATE programme and the BSc programme in Civil and Architectural Engineering through laboratory teaching, workshops, and co-supervision of student projects

 

Focus Area and Research Project

The research will develop new approaches to timber upcycling that minimise waste, extend carbon storage and advance circular construction. It will connect architectural design, material engineering and robotic fabrication to transform discarded timber into durable building components, developing lamination and bonding techniques alongside computational methods for design and structural optimisation.

The project builds on SDU CREATE’s previous research, including Re-VoxLam Truss and Re:Bridge, which explore how reclaimed timber can be reconstituted into structurally efficient architectural systems. Applicants are encouraged to consult the associated publications on reclaimed voxel lamination and stock and stress informed design and fabrication.

The successful candidate(s) will contribute to selected areas according to their expertise, working within a team with complementary skills:

  • Computational design and material allocation informed by available timber stock

  • Development of lamination and bonding techniques for architectural components

  • Robotic tooling and fabrication process development

  • Machine learning for material assessment and property prediction

  • Finite element modelling, structural optimisation and experimental validation

  • Fabrication and testing of full scale architectural demonstrators

  • Evaluation of material efficiency, structural performance and environmental benefits

 

About SDU CREATE’s Research Environment

The Centre for Computational Research in Emergent Architectural Technology and Engineering, SDU CREATE, is led by Associate Professor Roberto Naboni. The Centre investigates advanced concepts and applications in architectural engineering, focusing on computational design, construction robotics, and material innovation. SDU CREATE brings together an international research team working across architectural engineering, computer science, robotics, materials science, and biology. Its research develops sustainable, regenerative approaches to designing and constructing the built environment.

Located within the Faculty of Engineering at the University of Southern Denmark, SDU CREATE provides advanced laboratory facilities for robotic fabrication, additive and subtractive manufacturing, mixed reality applications in design and construction, and structural and mechanical testing. The facilities include industrial robotic systems, computational design platforms, and equipment for the experimental testing of materials, components, and structures. This environment supports interdisciplinary collaboration and partnerships with academic and industrial institutions in Denmark and internationally. The candidate(s) will work within a research culture that combines computational development with physical experimentation and full scale construction.

SDU CREATE is a partner in CEBE, a ten-year national research initiative funded by the Villum Foundation, in which Danish technical universities collaborate to advance the sustainability of the built environment within planetary boundaries. Within this initiative, SDU CREATE leads research in Digitalisation and Automation, RF4, and contributes to research in Design for Regeneration, Circularity, and Longevity, RF2. The programme provides a long-term research framework, access to national research networks, and opportunities for collaboration with academic and industrial partners.

 

Responsibilities

The successful candidate(s) will contribute to the development and delivery of CREATE’s research activities and laboratory-based investigations. Responsibilities include:

  • Conducting high-quality research within the defined research project and contributing original, scientifically rigorous outcomes

  • Conducting fabrication and structural testing experiments, including operation of robotic systems and laboratory equipment as relevant to the candidate’s research profile

  • Participating in CREATE’s research team activities, contributing to the development of design, fabrication, and testing frameworks

  • Developing and maintaining computational tools and workflows supporting the research activities

  • Assisting in teaching bachelor’s and master’s level courses and workshops, including co-supervision of thesis students and collaboration with interns in research-related activities

  • Disseminating research results through high-impact peer-reviewed publications and recognised international conferences

  • Sharing research outcomes through curated and high-quality outputs for digital platforms, exhibitions, and competitions

  • Contributing to the further development and maintenance of CREATE’s laboratory infrastructures and experimental facilities

  • Engaging with academic and industrial collaborators at the national and international level, including participation in the Villum CEBE research network

  • Assisting senior staff in the preparation of applications for external research funding

Engagement in these activities will evolve with the experience of the candidate(s), contributing to the Centre’s excellence and supporting their academic development, ideally towards future career advancement.

 

Candidate Requirements

Applications are invited from highly motivated candidates holding a Master’s degree in architecture, civil or architectural engineering, robotics, mechanical engineering, materials science, or other relevant disciplines related to the research areas. Candidates must demonstrate primary expertise in either Computational Design and Robotic Fabrication or AI-driven Computational Engineering, together with the ability to contribute to shared design, fabrication and validation activities.

Candidates must demonstrate:

  • Documented interest and foundational knowledge in circular construction, timber engineering or material upcycling

  • Competence in Grasshopper and Rhino, advanced for the Computational Design and Robotic Fabrication profile and at working level for the AI-driven Computational Engineering profile, together with relevant programming skills such as Python or C#

  • For the Computational Design and Robotic Fabrication profile: practical experience in robotic fabrication and development of computational design workflows; experience developing robotic tools, fixtures or fabrication procedures is particularly valued

  • For the AI-driven Computational Engineering profile: competence in finite element analysis and structural optimisation; practical experience developing and evaluating machine learning models is particularly valued

  • Hands-on laboratory experience with fabrication, including physical prototyping or specimen preparation, and experimental testing relevant to the selected profile

  • Demonstrated capacity to conduct, document, and disseminate projects and research outcomes suitable for peer-reviewed publication

  • Strong proficiency in English, both written and oral

  • Strong ability to work effectively within interdisciplinary teams and to coordinate and collaborate daily

  • Strong communication skills across graphical, written, and oral formats

  • A proven track record of involvement in research or innovation projects; experience in teaching assistance, peer-reviewed publications or engagement with academic or industry stakeholders is evaluated positively

 

Contact information

For further information about the position(s) and SDU CREATE’s activities, please contact the Head of Centre, Associate Professor Roberto Naboni, at ron@iti.sdu.dk. For additional information on the Centre’s work, visit www.create-sdu.com.

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

title: Service Technician and Installation Supervisor - Denmark
description:
About the position:
Ferrum is looking for an experienced and hands-on Service Technician and Installation Supervisor who can take responsibility for the installation, start-up and servicing of individual machines and complete filling lines at our customers' sites. We supply solutions for the production and filling of beer and soft drinks, including process equipment, filling machines, conveyors and associated utility systems.

You will have a key role at customer sites, combining hands-on work with the coordination of installation, connection, testing and commissioning activities. The position requires solid industry experience and extensive travel. Assignments will mainly be in Denmark and elsewhere in Europe, and you must be prepared for overnight stays, changing working hours and work carried out during production shutdowns.

Your main responsibilities:
- Plan and carry out the installation, mechanical assembly and run-in of new machines and complete filling lines.
- Act as Installation Supervisor and coordinate Ferrum technicians, customer personnel, subcontractors and other equipment suppliers on site.
- Ensure correct positioning, levelling and mechanical integration of machines, conveyors, piping, platforms and associated equipment.
- Carry out and verify pneumatic connections and assist with the connection of process media and utilities such as compressed air, water, CO2, nitrogen, steam, cooling and CIP.
- Participate in testing, FAT/SAT, commissioning, production start-up and performance runs in close cooperation with project management, automation specialists and the customer.
- Systematically troubleshoot mechanical and pneumatic faults and carry out basic fault-finding on electrical signals, sensors, drives and PLC-related issues.
- Perform service, inspections, preventive maintenance, repairs, modifications and format changeovers on existing systems.
- Identify the root causes of downtime and quality issues and recommend spare parts, maintenance activities and technical improvements.
- Train customer operators and maintenance personnel in safe operation, cleaning, changeovers and routine maintenance.
- Document progress, working hours, deviations, outstanding items and completed work in daily site and service reports.
- Ensure that all work is performed safely and in accordance with applicable safety requirements, customer site rules and relevant hygiene and food-production requirements.
- Provide practical feedback to the project, engineering and service teams to support the continuous improvement of future solutions and installations.

Your professional background:
- You have a relevant technical qualification, for example as an industrial mechanic, marine engineer, metal fabricator, automation technician or similar.
- Extensive relevant industry experience may compensate for a different educational background.
- You have several years of hands-on experience with the installation, servicing and commissioning of machinery or complete lines for the beverage, brewery, food or packaging industry.
- You have in-depth knowledge of filling lines and preferably experience with fillers, cappers, can seamers, conveyors, mixers/carbonators, pasteurisation, CIP and utility equipment.
- Experience from a manufacturer or service organisation such as Krones, KHS, Sidel, GEA or another supplier of process and filling lines would be a clear advantage.
- You are able to read and work from mechanical drawings, layouts, P&IDs, pneumatic diagrams, manuals and technical documentation.
- You have strong mechanical expertise and can perform precise alignment, installation, adjustment and systematic troubleshooting.
- Knowledge of electrical systems, instrumentation, variable frequency drives, sensors and Siemens PLC/HMI systems is an advantage, but this is not a dedicated PLC programming role.
- You can communicate professionally in written and spoken English. Danish or another European language would be an advantage.
- You hold a valid driving licence and a valid EU/EEA passport, and are able to travel and work throughout Denmark and Europe without significant restrictions.

Personal qualities:
- You take ownership of your assignments and maintain an overview, even when schedules are tight or several disciplines are working simultaneously.
- You are hands-on, solution-oriented and comfortable working independently away from the office.
- You communicate clearly and respectfully with customers, colleagues and subcontractors and can lead site meetings in a professional manner.
- You work in a structured manner and follow up on agreements, open items, safety, quality and documentation.
- You are flexible regarding travel, working hours and changing priorities and understand that start-ups and production-critical service assignments may require additional effort.

We offer:
- A permanent position with significant influence on the successful delivery of international customer projects.
- A varied working day involving new installations, commissioning, service and technical problem-solving.
- The opportunity to work with complete solutions - from process systems and utilities to the finished filling line.
- Close cooperation with project managers, engineers, automation specialists, suppliers and customers' technical organisations.
- An informal company with short decision-making paths, a high level of responsibility and a strong focus on quality and professional integrity.
- Salary and employment terms based on qualifications, together with relevant travel conditions and work equipment.

Practical information:
- Work location: Ferrum's base in Fredericia, combined with assignments at customer sites in Denmark and elsewhere in Europe.
- Travel: Extensive and varying according to the project portfolio. Overnight travel and assignments lasting several weeks may occur.
- Employment: Permanent position.

Application:
Please send your application and CV, including a brief description of your experience with filling lines, installation, service and commissioning. Please also state which machine types and suppliers you have previously worked with and the level of travel you are accustomed to.

For more information about the position and application process, please visit: https://workindenmark.jobnet.dk/find-job/3d290357-17fd-4f50-9711-71a9b19dd200

You will bring experience and judgement that strengthen the whole function, with the ambition and potential to be considered for the Head of People & Culture role within three to four years. We also welcome experienced former Heads of People & Culture who want to contribute at this level as an individual contributor.

You will serve the whole organisation, where you will partner closely with senior leaders on organisational, leadership, performance and people questions. You will also take responsibility for selected People & Culture priorities and projects across Impact Fund Denmark.

You will be a senior sparring partner to the Head of People & Culture and Executive Management, bringing the confidence and experience to challenge established thinking, shape our people strategy and lead its implementation. We expect you to contribute expertise that colleagues across People & Culture, including its leadership, can learn from.

You will report to our Head of People & Culture.

What you’ll be working on

A part of your role will be spent working directly with leaders across our investment organisation. The questions will vary: how a team should be structured, what capabilities we need next, how to address and build performance, how we strengthen succession, or what senior management needs to know before making a people decision.

You will:

  • lead culture and organisational development initiatives, translating our values and strategic priorities into everyday leadership behaviours, stronger collaboration and clear accountability for performance

  • advise senior leaders and Executive Management on organisational, capability, performance and complex people matters across headquarters and regional offices

  • prepare analysis, recommendations and decision material for Executive Management and, when relevant, the Board

  • support organisational and job design as teams, mandates and responsibilities evolve

  • advise on employee relations matters within local employment law and our agreements across headquarters and regional offices

  • use people data to identify patterns, challenge assumptions and support better decisions

  • take ownership of selected People & Culture projects that cut across the organisation

  • work with People Operations, Finance and Legal to ensure that people processes have clear approvals, appropriate controls and traceable documentation, supporting compliance and auditability under the Danish standards on public-sector auditing (SOR)

  • work closely with colleagues in Recruitment, People Operations and People Development, and coach and mentor People & Culture colleagues to strengthen their business partnering skills and prepare them for broader responsibilities

We are currently a relatively lean People & Culture function. That means there is not a specialist team to hand work over to. If a recommendation requires analysis, a presentation, a new process or careful implementation, you should be comfortable taking ownership and doing that work yourself.

What a good first year looks like

After your first year, we would expect that:

  • Change has moved beyond discussion and design. You have taken ownership of important organisational or capability priorities and helped turn them into practical improvements.

  • Core processes work well. Performance, talent and compensation processes in your area are consistent, useful and delivered on time. Leaders can explain and document their decisions, and demonstrate that people resources are used responsibly and effectively in a state-owned organisation.

  • Leaders trust your advice and judgement. Senior investment leaders involve you early as a trusted advisor and challenger when important organisational or people questions arise.

  • Decisions are better supported. Executive Management receives clear, well-argued recommendations and useful People material from you.

What we’re looking for

There is no single background that will make someone successful in this role, but you will need substantial experience dealing with the full People & Culture agenda, strategy and policy work, senior stakeholders and an organisation that has really great people and leaders with massive potential.

We would expect you to bring:

  • substantial experience in a broad senior HR Business Partner, People Partner or People leadership role in international organisations

  • experience advising senior executives directly on organisational and people decisions

  • demonstrated experience across the full HR agenda, including people strategy, culture and organisational development, recruitment, leadership development, performance, talent and succession, reward, employee relations and HR governance

  • practical experience with organisational design and complex employee matters

  • strong analytical skills and an ability to turn complicated information into a clear point of view and useful recommendations

  • evidence that you can take work from diagnosis through to implementation rather than relying on large specialist teams

  • solid knowledge of Danish employment law and HR practice; knowledge of local employment law across our regional offices is considered an advantage

  • professional fluency in Danish and English

It would be useful, but is not essential, if you also have experience with one or more of the following:

  • financial services, investment or another complex, knowledge-intensive organisation.

  • working with Executive teams and Boards or preparing material for Executives and Board discussions

  • international HR

  • a lean or smaller organisation where senior People professionals remain in delivery

  • compensation, People Analytics, talent or succession

Where the role sits

This is a senior individual-contributor role with no direct reports.

You will be the main People & Culture partner for our investment organisation, working directly with senior investment leaders. At the same time, you will own selected priorities that matter across Impact Fund Denmark and work closely with the Head of People & Culture.

The role will suit someone who likes that combination: being in the room for senior discussions, then staying close enough to the work to make sure something actually happens afterwards.

You should be comfortable moving between an Executive Management discussion, detailed analysis and the practical conversations needed to implement a decision.

Why join Impact Fund Denmark?

You will have close access to the Head of People & Culture and senior leaders across our organisation. You will have considerable scope to influence how we organise, lead and develop our people as Impact Fund Denmark grows and consolidates.

You will also be joining at a point where the organisation is evolving. We are building the people foundation for a larger and more professional international investor, which means some things are already well established while others still need to be shaped.

And the organisation's purpose is tangible. Our investments support green energy and infrastructure, financial services, sustainable food systems and healthcare in developing countries.

Practical details

  • Position: Permanent, full-time, 39 hours per week including lunch

  • Hybrid working: We currently have up to 20% of working time from home starting after 6 months of employment. We believe being in office is important for successful onboarding and integration into team and organisation.

About Impact Fund Denmark

Impact Fund Denmark (IFU – the Investment Fund for Developing Countries) is a Danish impact investor contributing to green, just and inclusive societies as well as supporting the Sustainable Development Goals. Impact Fund Denmark provides risk capital to companies operating in developing countries across Africa, Asia, Latin America and parts of Europe. Investments are made on commercial terms in the form of equity, loans and guarantees. Impact Fund Denmark has co-invested in over 1,300 companies in more than 100 developing countries and emerging markets. Contracted investments total EUR 31 billion, of which Impact Fund Denmark has contributed EUR 3.4 billion. Capital under management will be growing from EUR 2.1 billion to EUR 5.0 billion over the next few years. Read more at Impact Fund Denmark

title: Senior Talent Acquisition Partner
employer: Impact Fund Denmark (tidl. Investeringsfonden for Udviklingslande)
description:
Impact Fund Denmark has grown over the past few years, and many of our colleagues are still relatively new to the organisation. In 2027, our focus is on making that growth work well: strengthening the systems, processes and ways of working a larger organisation needs, while continuing to hire for our ambitions toward our 2027-2030 strategy.

Recruitment is an important part of that next phase.

We are creating a dedicated Senior Talent Acquisition Partner role to take ownership of how recruitment works across Impact Fund Denmark from attraction and sourcing to assessment, candidate experience and offer.

Hiring managers make the final hiring decision. Your role is to make sure they reach it through a strong, well-run and well-informed process.

You will report to our Head of People & Culture.

What you’ll be working on

You will own end-to-end recruitment across the organisation, covering both investment roles and corporate and support functions.

For each hire, you will take the process from the first conversation with the hiring manager through to offer. You will be responsible for keeping the process moving, maintaining a high standard and making sure both candidates and hiring managers know what to expect.

At the same time, you are responsible for anchoring the recruitment process in the organisation, training hiring manager or appointed recruitment panel, and meticulous documentation of the hiring process and decisions to ensure compliance.

That includes:

  • advising hiring managers on role definition, the candidate market and the right recruitment approach

  • delivering a professional and engaging candidate journey from start to finish, including a welcoming, seamless and positive on-site experience for arriving candidates

  • coordinating, overseeing and driving end-to-end recruitment processes in close collaboration with hiring managers

  • sourcing directly, mapping relevant markets and reaching out to candidates who may not be actively looking

  • Identifying, sourcing and vetting talents on different channels to find top-tier active and passive candidates, and conduct initial screening interviews to assess technical and interpersonal-skills as well as cultural alignment

  • screening and interviewing candidates and helping managers design structured, relevant assessments

  • managing timelines, expectations and communication from intake through to offer

  • briefing and managing external search or recruitment partners when we use them

  • setting and ensuring a consistent standard for job ads, interviews, candidate communication and hiring documentation

  • building talent pipelines and market knowledge for recurring or difficult-to-fill profiles

  • using recruitment data to improve hiring quality, timeliness and cost-effectiveness, and demonstrate responsible use of recruitment resources in a state-owned organisation

  • improving our recruitment tools, templates and ways of working over time

  • ensuring that selection criteria, candidate assessments, approvals and hiring decisions are clearly documented and traceable, supporting public-sector governance, compliance with applicable rules and internal policies, and auditability under the Danish standards on public-sector auditing (SOR)

  • contributing to selected People & Culture projects alongside recruitment where it makes sense

  • training and guiding hiring managers on recruitment processes and guidelines to drive fair, consistent hiring decisions

We use Talentech as our applicant tracking system and CatalystOne as our HR system.

What a good first year looks like

After your first year, we would expect that:

  • Recruitment has a clear owner. Hiring managers know where to go for advice and support, and there is a consistent professional standard across the organisation.

  • Processes are stronger and more consistent. Roles are well defined, assessments are structured, and recruitment decisions are properly documented.

  • Hiring processes keeps moving. Managers receive relevant, well-screened candidate fields, and processes keep momentum on the factors within your control.

  • We rely less on who happens to apply. Direct sourcing is used actively where needed, and external search partners are brought in selectively and managed closely.

What we’re looking for

This role needs someone who is comfortable owning recruitment rather than simply coordinating it.

You will need to bring:

  • Solid experience independently managing end-to-end recruitment

  • strong direct-sourcing experience, including outreach to passive candidates

  • experience recruiting into a professional, knowledge-intensive environment

  • confidence advising senior and demanding hiring managers

  • the ability to keep recruitment processes moving and hold people to agreed timelines

  • experience screening and interviewing candidates, with good judgement about assessment quality

  • strong structure, follow-through and attention to the documentation behind hiring decisions

  • professional fluency in Danish and English

It would be useful, but is not essential, if you also have experience with one or more of the following:

  • recruiting investment or financial-services professionals

  • executive search or other senior professional recruitment

  • briefing and managing external search or recruitment partners

  • market mapping, talent intelligence or proactive pipeline building

  • using recruitment data and metrics to improve processes

  • international recruitment

Where the role sits

This is a Lead role with no direct reports. You will have full ownership of the recruitment lifecycle, meaning you should be comfortable balancing high-level strategy and manager coaching with hands-on execution, including the day-to-day administrative and coordination tasks, candidate care and operational execution.

You will be the main point of contact for recruitment across Impact Fund Denmark and the person responsible for how recruitment is run and for its quality.

Hiring managers remain accountable for who they hire. You bring the candidate market knowledge, recruitment expertise and process that help them make those decisions well.

That means being willing to challenge a brief when necessary, being realistic about the market, keeping a process moving when other priorities compete for attention, and making sure candidate experience does not become an afterthought.

For specialist searches, or during periods of particularly high hiring activity, you will also work with HRBP colleagues and external search partners. For periods of low activity you will build adjacent HR capabilities and part take in leadership development,....

Why join Impact Fund Denmark?

You will have the opportunity to shape how recruitment is done across the organisation rather than inherit a narrowly defined part of the process.

You will work closely with the Head of People & Culture and with senior leaders across the organisation, including our investment teams.

The role is unusually broad for an internal recruitment position. One search may be for an investment professional with a highly specialised background; the next may be for a corporate or functional expert.

And the work connects directly to Impact Fund Denmark's purpose. Every person you help bring into the organisation contributes, in some way, to investments in green energy and infrastructure, financial services, sustainable food systems and healthcare in developing countries.
